item.title: Supporting Pacific athletes to go for gold
item.content:
The Australian Government is investing in the next generation of Pacific sporting talent on their journey to the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

Australia will provide $15.6 million over 4 years to support athletes and officials from 14 Pacific countries to access high-performance training and qualification opportunities to compete at major international sporting events.

In partnership with the Australian Olympic Committee, Paralympics Australia, Commonwealth Games Australia and regional organisations, the funding will maximise Pacific athletes and officials’ participation and opportunities for success.

Pacific athletes and officials will be supported for the Tahiti 2027 Pacific Games, the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games and the Rarotonga 2029 Pacific Mini Games and other international sporting events.

This continues Australia’s work with Australian and regional sporting organisations to increase Pacific participation in major games.

This partnership reflects Australia’s commitment to ensure Pacific athletes have every opportunity to compete, succeed and leave a sustained legacy that contributes to continued Pacific sporting excellence.

Quotes attributable to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese

“The Pacific is home to incredible sporting talent. This new partnership will contribute to producing the next generation of successful athletes.

“As we move forward in planning for Brisbane 2032 Australia looks forward to welcoming the best of the best sporting talent from the Pacific and supporting them to go for gold.”

Quotes attributable to Minister Pat Conroy

“Sport has a unique power to bring people together, and support healthy lives, gender equity and youth leadership.

“This is an investment in the development of athletes across the Pacific. I look forward to seeing many successful Pacific athletes at the upcoming Paralympics, Commonwealth and Olympic Games.”
